> **Entire cohort — all tumour stages.** This page runs the same analysis as the Local/Early page on the **unrestricted** cohort: **N = 943** (322 Local/Early + 621 Advanced/Metastatic; 596 carboplatin, 347 cisplatin). It reads `ritu_full_master.rds`, saved by `ritu_data.qmd` immediately before the stage restriction, so every variable is identical — including the creatinine from the 2022P001091 RPDR pull and the CKD / ESKD / AKI family.
>
> **`tumor_stage` is a covariate again here.** It is constant in the Local/Early cohort and therefore dropped there; in the entire cohort it varies, so it is restored to Table 1 and to every Fine-Gray, cause-specific, Cox and linear-subHR adjuster set. That makes this page's model specification the same as the Jiaxuan project's.
>
> **Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page.** AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 4, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd) and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. **Read both models with their event counts in view** — 197 AKI and 70 CKD-composite events in 943 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See `RITU_PROJECT.md`.

# 1 Setup {.content-hidden}

```{r}
#| label: setup-ritu-entire
# Force UTF-8 locale so kable captions and other strings render real Unicode
# (e.g. em-dash) instead of <U+2014> escape sequences.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8"))
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidycmprsk)
library(ggsurvfit)
library(gtsummary)
library(flextable)
library(rvg)
library(officer)
library(patchwork)

# Output directory for downloadable Word tables (placed under docs/ so the
# rendered website can serve them from ../tables/entire/<name>.docx).
docx_dir <- "docs/tables/entire"
dir.create(docx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Output directory for editable PowerPoint copies of every figure. A knitr
# plot hook (defined below) saves last_plot() to docs/pptx/entire/<label>.pptx
# and appends a download link after the figure in the rendered HTML.
dir.create("docs/pptx/entire", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pptx_dir <- normalizePath("docs/pptx/entire", mustWork = TRUE)
# Relative path for download links from rendered docs/qmd/*.html
pptx_rel_prefix <- "../pptx/entire/"

# Persist the chunk-label -> pptx-path mapping so the chunk hook can emit
# the download link only when the .pptx was actually written.
.pptx_written <- new.env()
.pptx_pair    <- new.env()

# Save one ggplot to <path> as an editable PPTX (rvg::dml).
.save_pptx <- function(p, path) {
  tryCatch({
    doc <- officer::read_pptx()
    doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content",
                              master = "Office Theme")
    doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, rvg::dml(ggobj = p),
                            location = officer::ph_location_type(type = "body"))
    print(doc, target = path)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

# fig.process runs in the chunk eval context. For stacked helpers, the helper
# stashes .pptx_pair[[label]] = list(default=p, fine=p_fine) so we can write
# two PPTX files. Otherwise fall back to last_plot() and one file.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(filename) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(filename)
  pair <- .pptx_pair[[label]]
  if (!is.null(pair) && inherits(pair$default, "ggplot") && inherits(pair$fine, "ggplot")) {
    p1 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
    p2 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    ok1 <- .save_pptx(pair$default, p1)
    ok2 <- .save_pptx(pair$fine,    p2)
    rels <- c(if (ok1) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx"),
              if (ok2) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    if (length(rels)) .pptx_written[[label]] <- rels
    return(filename)
  }
  p <- tryCatch(ggplot2::last_plot(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(p) || !inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(filename)
  pptx_path <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
  if (.save_pptx(p, pptx_path)) {
    .pptx_written[[label]] <- paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx")
  }
  filename
})

# A "chunk" hook fires after the whole chunk is rendered: append download link(s).
local({
  default_chunk_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
    out <- default_chunk_hook(x, options)
    label <- options$label
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.pptx_written[[label]])) {
      rel <- .pptx_written[[label]]
      if (length(rel) == 2) {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download top plot as PowerPoint</a> · <a href="%s" download>📊 Download bottom (10 %% ticks)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1], rel[2])
      } else {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download as PowerPoint (editable)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1])
      }
      out <- paste0(out, link)
    }
    out
  })
})

# Save a gtsummary table to a Word document.
# --- Sparse-outcome guard (Ritu cohort) --------------------------------------
# Some outcomes can still be too sparse for a ~20-covariate model even in the
# entire cohort. A model that cannot be
# estimated raises an error, which would abort the entire render, so every
# table / row / figure helper is wrapped below. On success the output is exactly
# what the Jiaxuan version produces; on failure a short note is emitted in place
# of the table or figure. No model specification is changed.
.wrap_tbl <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e) knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-warning}\n",
    "## Model not estimable in this cohort\n\n",
    "Too few events among the ", nrow(dat), " patients to fit ",
    "this model with the full adjuster set.\n\n",
    "Error: `", conditionMessage(e), "`\n:::\n")))
}
.wrap_row <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(time_var, status_var, label, ...) tryCatch(
    f(time_var, status_var, label, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      ev <- tryCatch(
        sum(as.character(dat[[status_var]]) == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
        error = function(e2) NA_integer_)
      tibble::tibble(
        Outcome = label, Model = "not estimable",
        N = NA_integer_, `Excluded (missing cov.)` = NA_integer_,
        Events = as.integer(ev),
        `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = "not estimable", `p-value` = "\u2014")
    })
}
.wrap_plot <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e)
    ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, size = 3.4, lineheight = 1.3,
        label = paste0("Model not estimable in this cohort\n",
                       "(too few events among the ", nrow(dat),
                       " patients)\n\n",
                       strwrap(conditionMessage(e), width = 60,
                               prefix = "\n", initial = ""))) +
      ggplot2::theme_void())
}

save_tbl_docx <- function(tbl, docx_name) {
  ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(tbl)
  flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(docx_dir,
                                               paste0(docx_name, ".docx")))
  invisible(tbl)
}

# Load the entire (unrestricted, all-stage) cohort produced by ritu_data.qmd
dat <- readRDS("ritu_full_master.rds")

# Create eGFR ratio: CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (unindexed) / Cockcroft-Gault
# Also create per-10 mL/min rescaled versions of cockcroft and CKD-EPI for
# reporting (HRs per 1 mL/min are clinically uninterpretable; convention in
# nephro-onc is per 10 mL/min — bio_agent confirmed). Adjusters keep raw scale.
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # Ratio uses UNCAPPED eGFR
    egfr_ratio    = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / cockcroft,
    egfr_ratio_per10 = -egfr_ratio * 10,  # per 0.1-unit *decrease* reporting scale
    egfr_discrepancy = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft,
    # per-10-mL/min DECLINE reporting scale for eGFR discrepancy: HR for this
    # variable reads as the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower
    # discrepancy (i.e., when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is 10 mL/min farther below CG).
    egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10,
    # Sensitivity-analysis eGFR ratio (Section 11):
    # numerator = CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C only (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed)
    # denominator = CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine only (baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed)
    # (Both unindexed; the ratio itself is invariant to whether indexed or unindexed
    # because BSA cancels.) per10 below is the per-0.1 DECLINE reporting scale.
    egfr_ratio_sens       = baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_ratio_sens_per10 = -egfr_ratio_sens * 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR (new primary exposure):
    # egfr_diff_pct = 100 * (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed - Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault
    # egfr_diff_pct_per10: HR reads as multiplicative change per 10 percentage-point DECLINE.
    egfr_diff_pct         = 100 * (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft) / cockcroft,
    egfr_diff_pct_per10   = -egfr_diff_pct / 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR for sensitivity analysis:
    # numerator - denominator = CKD-EPI 2012 CysC - CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, both unindexed.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens        = 100 * (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed - baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed) / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10  = -egfr_diff_pct_sens / 10,
    cockcroft_per10 = cockcroft / 10,
    ckd_epi_per10   = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / 10
  )
```

# 2 Table 1: Baseline Characteristics (Overall + Cisplatin / Carboplatin)

Table 1 is now stratified by `platin_group`. Columns show the overall cohort, the cisplatin subgroup, and the carboplatin subgroup side-by-side, with a between-group p-value in the final column (Wilcoxon rank-sum for continuous, Fisher exact for categorical with expected cell < 5, else χ²). The `platin_group`, `carbo_AUC`, and `cis_dose`-related variables are removed from the row list because they are collinear with the stratification column.

**Missing counts.** `missing = "ifany"` — each variable's Unknown row appears only when the variable actually has missing values in that column. In practice this cohort is complete on the entire adjuster / predictor set once record 911 is dropped upstream in `ritu_data.qmd`: `pre_HGB_45days`, `pre_PLT_45days`, `pre_ALB_45days`, and `pre_CRE_45days` all show 0/943 missing, and the age / sex / BMI / smoking / thyroid / steroids / RPDR-comorbidity / eGFR variables are also fully populated. The only NA-by-design variables in the row list are `carbo_AUC` / `carbo_AUC_cat` (NA for cisplatin patients) and `cis_dose` / `cis_dose_high` (NA for carboplatin patients). Consequently, the "Excluded (missing cov.)" column in the Section 4 / 7 / 11 summary tables is 0 for every outcome.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-table1-entire
dat %>%
  # Show the numeric KDIGO stage as a labelled factor for Table 1. get_ckd_stage()
  # collapses G3a/G3b into a single stage 3, unlike ckd_stage_cre / ckd_stage_cre_cys.
  mutate(ckd_stage_baseline = droplevels(
           factor(ckd_stage_baseline, levels = 1:5,
                  labels = c("G1 (>=90)", "G2 (60-89)", "G3 (30-59)",
                             "G4 (15-29)", "G5 (<15)")))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    age, age_cat, sex, race, ethnicity, tumor_stage, cancer_type_cat_7,
    platin_group, carbo_AUC, carbo_AUC_cat, cis_dose, cis_dose_high,
    ici, Bevacizumab, Paclitaxel, Pemetrexed, Doxorubicin, Etoposide,
    Gemcitabine, Pertuzumab, Trastuzumab, Docetaxel, other_chemo, Administered_alone,
    hiv_rpdr, thyroid, smoking, steroids, esrd_kt,
    cci, score, ecog_score, bmi, bmi_cat,
    pre_HGB_45days, pre_PLT_45days, pre_ALB_45days, pre_CRE_45days,
    baseline_cys_c, baseline_cre, cr_cys,
    baseline_cre_egfr, baseline_cys_c_egfr,
    ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex,
    ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys,
    cockcroft, egfr_ratio,
    # Long-horizon kidney variables (Sections 5.16-5.19 of ritu_data.qmd).
    # eGFR_CRE_baseline / ckd_stage_baseline are baseline; last_cre_days is
    # creatinine follow-up length; the rest are outcomes over that full window,
    # NOT censored at 90 days like every other outcome in this project.
    eGFR_CRE_baseline, ckd_stage_baseline, last_cre_days,
    aki, aki_any, ckd_incidence, ckd_incidence_any, ckd_progression,
    eskd_defination_1, esrd_kt_after_ici, eskd_composite, ckd_composite
  ) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = platin_group,
    statistic = list(age ~ "{mean} ({sd})"),
    missing = "ifany"
  ) %>%
  add_overall(last = FALSE) %>%
  add_p() %>%
  modify_header(label ~ "**Characteristic**") %>%
  modify_spanning_header(all_stat_cols() ~ "**Platinum group**")
```

## 2.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)

`days_last_follow_up` = `last_follow_up_date − baseline_sample_date`. Four alternative definitions of "follow-up time" are shown side-by-side so the reader can pick the most defensible one for their purpose:

- **A — Raw days**: unrestricted calendar follow-up (median dominated by patients who kept returning for years).
- **B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days**: restricts to patients whose last-known contact was **within 1 year** of baseline (drops the long tail of years-later return visits; more comparable across patients).
- **C — Analytic, capped at 90 days**: `min(days_last_follow_up, 90)` — the 90-day window the adverse-event and hospitalization outcomes were abstracted in.
- **D — Analytic (capped at 90) & ≤ 365 days raw**: same as C but excluding the long-tail returners.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-followup-desc-entire
followup_summary <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, platin_group, days_last_follow_up) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(days_last_follow_up)

fmt_med_iqr <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
}

groups_split <- function(f) {
  x_all <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up)
  x_cis <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up[followup_summary$platin_group == "Cisplatin"])
  x_car <- f(followup_summary$days_last_follow_up[followup_summary$platin_group == "Carboplatin"])
  list(Overall = x_all, Cisplatin = x_cis, Carboplatin = x_car)
}

fu_row <- function(label, xs) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Interpretation                      = label,
    `Overall N`                         = length(xs$Overall),
    `Overall — Median [IQR] (days)`     = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Overall),
    `Cisplatin N`                       = length(xs$Cisplatin),
    `Cisplatin — Median [IQR] (days)`   = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Cisplatin),
    `Carboplatin N`                     = length(xs$Carboplatin),
    `Carboplatin — Median [IQR] (days)` = fmt_med_iqr(xs$Carboplatin)
  )
}

def_A <- function(v) v
def_B <- function(v) v[v <= 365]
def_C <- function(v) pmin(v, 90)
def_D <- function(v) pmin(v[v <= 365], 90)

followup_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fu_row("A — Raw days",                                   groups_split(def_A)),
  fu_row("B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days",                       groups_split(def_B)),
  fu_row("C — Analytic (capped at 90 days), whole cohort", groups_split(def_C)),
  fu_row("D — Analytic (capped at 90 days), ≤ 365 days",   groups_split(def_D))
)

flextable::flextable(followup_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption("Follow-up time from baseline to last known status (whole cohort). Four alternative definitions shown side-by-side.") |>
  flextable::autofit()
```

## 2.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the [ICI-CKD project](https://tianqi-ouyang.github.io/ICI-CKD-/data_management.html)
and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd). Creatinine
for these comes from the newer 2022P001091 RPDR pull.

> **These are the only outcomes on this page that are not censored at 90 days.**
> A qualifying CKD episode has to be *sustained for ≥ 90 days*, so they run over
> the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up rather than the 90-day window used
> by every model above and below. They are reported descriptively here and are
> **not** in any Fine-Gray, cause-specific or Cox model.

**Definitions as of the latest revision.** `aki` is now restricted to events
**within 1 year** of baseline (`aki_any` keeps the unrestricted count for
reference and is not modelled). `ckd_incidence` uses a **> 25 %** eGFR drop;
`ckd_incidence_any` drops the percent requirement entirely; `ckd_progression`
now additionally requires a **> 30 %** further drop, where it previously counted
any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD
as progression and is why that count fell sharply.

`aki` is also not the same variable as `AKI_g2_90days` / `AKI_kdigo_90days`: it
compares each creatinine against the patient's own preceding 90-day median (or
2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation
below shows how far the two diverge.

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/entire/sec2_kidney_longhorizon.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-kidney-lt
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

kidney_lt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .kid_row("aki",               "aki_days",                    "AKI within 1 year (serial creatinine)"),
  .kid_row("aki_any",           "aki_days_any",                "AKI at any time (reference only, not modelled)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence",     "time_to_ckd_incidence",       "CKD incidence (>25% eGFR drop to <60, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence_any", "time_to_ckd_incidence_any",   "CKD incidence any (>=60 to <60, sustained >=90d, no % drop)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_progression",   "time_to_ckd_progression",     "CKD progression (<60 at baseline, further >30% drop, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("esrd_kt_after_ici", NULL,                          "ESRD / kidney transplant after baseline"),
  .kid_row("eskd_composite",    "time_to_eskd_composite",      "ESKD composite"),
  .kid_row("ckd_composite",     "time_to_ckd_composite",       "CKD composite (incidence + progression + ESKD composite)")
)

ft_kid <- flextable::flextable(kidney_lt) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(
    "Long-horizon kidney outcomes (N = %d). Not censored at 90 days.", nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_kid, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec2_kidney_longhorizon.docx"))
ft_kid
```

Creatinine follow-up actually available for these outcomes, and how the two AKI
definitions compare:

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-kidney-lt-fu
cat(sprintf("Days from baseline to last creatinine: median %.0f (IQR %.0f-%.0f), max %.0f\n",
            median(dat$last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(dat$last_cre_days, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            quantile(dat$last_cre_days, .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(dat$last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Patients with no post-baseline creatinine: %d\n",
            sum(is.na(dat$last_cre_days))))
cat("\nSerial-creatinine AKI (rows) vs 90-day KDIGO AKI (columns):\n")
print(table(`serial aki` = dat$aki, `AKI_kdigo_90days` = dat$AKI_kdigo_90days))
```


# 3 eGFR Ratio and Discordance Distributions (Overall)

## 3.1 eGFR Ratio distribution

Red bins highlight the region **below ratio = 1** (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys eGFR below Cockcroft-Gault, consistent with muscle-wasting / sarcopenia); gray bins are the region above.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-egfr-ratio-lt09-count
#| results: asis
n_lt <- sum(dat$egfr_ratio < 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
n_av <- sum(!is.na(dat$egfr_ratio))
cat(sprintf(
  "> **eGFR ratio < 0.9:** %d / %d (%.1f%%) of the whole cohort.\n",
  n_lt, n_av, 100 * n_lt / n_av))
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-egfr-ratio-hist
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
ratio_hist <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_ratio)) %>%
  mutate(side = ifelse(egfr_ratio < 1, "neg", "pos"))

ggplot(ratio_hist, aes(x = egfr_ratio, fill = side)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0,
                 color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Ratio (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed / Cockcroft-Gault)",
       x = "eGFR Ratio",
       y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## 3.2 eGFR Discordance distribution

Signed eGFR discordance = CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault (mL/min). Red bins highlight the negative side (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys **below** Cockcroft-Gault — the direction that flags reduced cystatin-based eGFR relative to creatinine-based, consistent with muscle wasting / sarcopenia); gray bins are the positive side.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-egfr-discordance-hist
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
disc_hist <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_discrepancy)) %>%
  mutate(side = ifelse(egfr_discrepancy < 0, "neg", "pos"))

ggplot(disc_hist, aes(x = egfr_discrepancy, fill = side)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 5, boundary = 0,
                 color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Discordance (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys − Cockcroft-Gault)",
       x = "eGFR Discordance (mL/min)",
       y = "Percent of Patients (%)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

## 3.3 eGFR Difference (%) distribution

Signed eGFR difference (%) = 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault. Concordance sits at 0 %. Red bins highlight the negative side (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys below CG by more than 0 %, consistent with muscle wasting / sarcopenia); gray bins are the positive side.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-egfr-diffpct-hist
#| fig-width: 8
```

# 4 Fine-Gray Models — Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (eGFR Difference (%) per 10 % decline, adjusted for Cockcroft-Gault)

Each table below shows univariable (one variable at a time) and multivariable Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratios side-by-side. A Word version of each table is saved during render — the download link sits under its heading.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-fg-helper
.adj_set <- function(pred_var, pre_labs, egfr_adj) {
  adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
           "cancer_type_cat_7","tumor_stage","platin_group","high_dose",
           "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
           "bmi","smoking","steroids","thyroid")
  # Drop platin_group when predictor requires dose data (carbo-only after drop_na)
  if (grepl("dose_discrep", pred_var)) adj <- setdiff(adj, "platin_group")
  if (egfr_adj == "cockcroft") adj <- c(adj, "cockcroft")
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi")   adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) adj <- c(adj, pre_labs)
  adj
}

# fg_model: returns univariable + multivariable merged Fine-Gray table.
# If docx_name is supplied, also saves the table as a .docx in docx_dir.
fg_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                     egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi"),
                     docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pred_var, pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  # Multivariable
  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- tidycmprsk::crr(fmla_mv, failcode = 1, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  # Univariable: one Fine-Gray fit per variable
  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = tidycmprsk::crr,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3),
      method.args = list(failcode = 1)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_model <- .wrap_tbl(fg_model)


# cox_model: same signature/output for the 90-day death analysis (Cox PH).
cox_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                      egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi"),
                      docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pred_var, pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- survival::coxph(fmla_mv, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = survival::coxph,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_model <- .wrap_tbl(cox_model)

```

## 4.1 AKI within 1 Year (Fine-Gray, death competing)

> **These are the only two outcomes modelled on this page.** Both run on the
> long-horizon kidney outcomes built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of
> [Data Management](ritu_data.qmd):
> AKI is administratively censored at **365 days**, the CKD composite runs to the
> **last creatinine** (day 0 → last follow-up). Death at any time is the
> competing event in both, taken from `death_days_any` rather than the 90-day
> `death_90` flag, which cannot place a death in time beyond day 90.
> `death_days_any` is the union of the two sources that carry a death date — the
> RPDR `Date_Of_Death` when there is one, otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up
> date for a patient REDCap records as dead. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR
> with no date who is still alive in REDCap stays censored.
>
> The predictor is `egfr_diff_pct_per10` (per 10 percentage-point decline in the
> eGFR difference), adjusted for Cockcroft-Gault plus the project's standard
> adjuster set (Section 1).

[📄 Download Word table](../tables/entire/sec4_aki_365.docx) · [CKD Composite](../tables/entire/sec4_ckd_composite.docx)

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-fg-aki365
fg_model("cmp_time_aki_365", "cmp_status_aki_365", "egfr_diff_pct_per10",
         egfr_adj = "cockcroft", docx_name = "sec4_aki_365")
```

## 4.2 CKD Composite, Any Time Post-Baseline (Fine-Gray, death competing)

CKD composite = CKD incidence (> 25 % eGFR drop to < 60, sustained ≥ 90 d)
**+** CKD progression (eGFR < 60 at baseline with a further > 30 % drop, sustained
≥ 90 d) **+** ESKD composite.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-fg-ckdcomposite
fg_model("cmp_time_ckd_composite", "cmp_status_ckd_composite", "egfr_diff_pct_per10",
         egfr_adj = "cockcroft", docx_name = "sec4_ckd_composite")
```

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-fg-lt-counts
lt_counts <- tibble::tibble(
  Outcome = c("AKI within 1 year", "CKD composite (any time)"),
  Censored = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 0), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 0)),
  Event    = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 1), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 1)),
  Death    = c(sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365 == 2), sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite == 2)),
  `Median follow-up (d)` = c(
    round(median(dat$cmp_time_aki_365, na.rm = TRUE)),
    round(median(dat$cmp_time_ckd_composite, na.rm = TRUE)))
)
knitr::kable(lt_counts, caption = sprintf(
  "Competing-risk event counts, N = %d. Status 0 = censored, 1 = event, 2 = death.",
  nrow(dat)))
```

# 6 CG vs CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (highlighted by Age / BMI)

For each plot below, the x-axis is Cockcroft-Gault eGFR (mL/min) and the y-axis is CKD-EPI Cr-Cys *unindexed* eGFR (mL/min). The dashed line is `y = x` (perfect agreement). Patients meeting the highlighted threshold are coloured red; all others are grey. `N` shown in each title is the count of patients with both eGFR values non-missing; `n_red` is the count meeting the red criterion.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-scatter-cg-epi-helper
plot_cg_vs_epi <- function(highlight_var, threshold, label) {
  d <- dat %>%
    filter(!is.na(cockcroft), !is.na(ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex),
           !is.na(.data[[highlight_var]])) %>%
    mutate(highlight = .data[[highlight_var]] >= threshold)

  n_total <- nrow(d)
  n_red   <- sum(d$highlight)

  # Fit two separate OLS models so we can annotate each with its equation + R².
  fit_true  <- lm(ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex ~ cockcroft,
                  data = d %>% filter(highlight))
  fit_false <- lm(ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex ~ cockcroft,
                  data = d %>% filter(!highlight))
  eq_str <- function(fit) {
    b  <- coef(fit)
    r2 <- summary(fit)$r.squared
    sprintf("y = %.2f x %+.1f   (R² = %.2f)", b[2], b[1], r2)
  }

  ggplot(d, aes(x = cockcroft, y = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex,
                color = highlight, fill = highlight)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
    # One OLS regression line per level of `highlight` (colour + CI ribbon
    # match the dot colour).
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
                alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = 5, y = 195, hjust = 0, size = 3.4,
             color = "#E31A1C", label = paste0(">= threshold: ", eq_str(fit_true))) +
    annotate("text", x = 5, y = 182, hjust = 0, size = 3.4,
             color = "grey40",  label = paste0("< threshold:  ", eq_str(fit_false))) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "#E31A1C"),
                       guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey60", "TRUE" = "#E31A1C"),
                      guide = "none") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 200), ylim = c(0, 200)) +
    labs(x = "Cockcroft-Gault eGFR (mL/min)",
         y = "CKD-EPI Cr-Cys eGFR, unindexed (mL/min)",
         title = sprintf("%s   |   N = %d, n_red = %d",
                         label, n_total, n_red)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
}
```

## 6.7 – 6.12 eGFR Difference (%) distribution by category

For each of the same six splits as 10.1 – 10.6, overlaid kernel density curves of the eGFR difference (%) = 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault. Red = highlighted level (≥ threshold, or Female for the sex panel); grey = reference level. Dashed grey vertical line marks the 0 % concordance point; dotted verticals mark each group's median. Subtitle carries N and median for each level plus a two-sided Mann-Whitney U p-value (equivalent to Wilcoxon rank-sum) comparing the two distributions.

```{r}
#| label: ritu-entire-ratio-by-group-helper
plot_ratio_by_group <- function(highlight_var, threshold, label,
                                highlight_label, reference_label) {
  d <- dat %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct), !is.na(.data[[highlight_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(grp = factor(
      ifelse(.data[[highlight_var]] >= threshold, highlight_label, reference_label),
      levels = c(highlight_label, reference_label)))

  med_tbl <- d %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grp) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(m = median(egfr_diff_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
                     n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  pval <- tryCatch(
    wilcox.test(egfr_diff_pct ~ grp, data = d)$p.value,
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  p_str <- if (is.na(pval)) "NA" else
    ifelse(pval < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", pval))

  col_vec <- setNames(c("#E31A1C", "grey50"),
                      c(highlight_label, reference_label))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = egfr_diff_pct, fill = grp, color = grp)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
    geom_vline(data = med_tbl, aes(xintercept = m, color = grp),
               linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = col_vec) +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_vec) +
    labs(x = "eGFR difference (%): 100 × (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys − CG) / CG",
         y = "Density",
         fill = NULL, color = NULL,
         title = label,
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "%s: N = %d, median = %.1f %%   |   %s: N = %d, median = %.1f %%   |   Mann-Whitney U p = %s",
           highlight_label,
           med_tbl$n[med_tbl$grp == highlight_label],
           med_tbl$m[med_tbl$grp == highlight_label],
           reference_label,
           med_tbl$n[med_tbl$grp == reference_label],
           med_tbl$m[med_tbl$grp == reference_label],
           p_str)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey25"))
}
```
